bull.b: A record customer-satisfaction score and repeated independent network recognition support durable customer acquisition and retention. Strong perceived network quality can reinforce share gains, reduce churn, and provide a foundation for monetizing recurring wireless and broadband relationships over coming quarters.

Growth in postpaid service revenue, total service revenue, and adjusted EBITDA indicates improving scale across recurring connectivity services. This combination supports operating leverage and strengthens the company’s ability to fund network investment, spectrum needs, and shareholder returns from internally generated earnings.

Large operating and free-cash-flow generation provides meaningful financial capacity for network investment, spectrum purchases, debt service, and capital returns. The raised free-cash-flow outlook also indicates that current profitability is translating into substantial cash resources over the medium term.

bear.b: Elevated leverage and declining equity reduce financial flexibility compared with a stronger balance sheet. Higher debt obligations can constrain capital allocation and make the company more sensitive to refinancing conditions, particularly while it preserves resources for future spectrum opportunities.

Although recent results are strong, uneven annual revenue performance and a history of negative free cash flow show that earnings and cash generation have not been consistently stable. Moderate current conversion also leaves less room for execution errors or heavier investment needs.

bear.t: Pressure in prepaid and wholesale businesses
bear.b: Declining prepaid activity and planned wholesale roll-offs create structural pressure in parts of the customer and revenue base outside core postpaid growth. These trends can limit diversification, reduce channel contribution, and require continued reliance on competitive execution in higher-value services.
